primitives.name: Discounted Cumulative Accuracy
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Metric: Discounted Cumulative Accuracy, DCA = Σ_{t=0}^{T} p_t(1 - t/T), with p_t = (1/N)Σ_n 1{|s_n - s*_n| = t} — exact accuracy at T=0, forgiving near-misses with linear discount as tolerance T grows (inspired by DCG from IR).
primitives.assumptions: Narrative contains complete scoring data; team attribution is unambiguous; exact point values are recoverable from action descriptions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When tolerance T approaches zero, DCA reduces to exact match accuracy; when T increases, penalizes larger errors less severely.

layer2.mapping: DCA mirrors information retrieval metrics like DCG, adapted for discrete numeric prediction tasks in sports narratives.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy scores under varying tolerance thresholds T ∈ {0,1,3,5,10}

primitives.name: Divide-and-Conquer Batching Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Strategies: monolithic (whole narrative at once) vs divide-and-conquer — split into batches of 1, 3, 10, 30 plays (DnC-{1,3,10,30}) or by player (DnC-P), aggregate partial sums.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'DnC-k': 'batch size parameter', 'k': 'number of plays per batch'}
primitives.assumptions: Partial aggregations are additive and independent; batch boundaries do not introduce bias in attribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Performance degrades if batch size exceeds context window or if inter-batch dependencies exist.

layer2.mapping: Batched processing enables scalable reasoning by reducing context load while preserving accuracy through aggregation.
layer2.telemetry: Accuracy improvement with increasing batch size (e.g., DnC-10 vs monolithic)

primitives.name: SportsGen Synthetic Narrative Generator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - SportsGen ablations: varying S:NS ratios, action counts per turn, and four symbolicness levels (Original → Scrambled teams → Fictional FIFA names → Symbolic "Player 1, 2, 3...").
primitives.assumptions: Synthetic narratives maintain statistical properties of real data; symbolic transformations preserve semantic structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Highly symbolic inputs may obscure entity identification, leading to hallucinations or misattribution.

layer2.mapping: Generates adversarial test cases to probe LLM robustness against hallucination and attribution failure.
layer2.telemetry: Human preference ratings and model performance on synthetic variants

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge lies in extracting numeric outcomes from sequential, unstructured narratives. The Discounted Cumulative Accuracy (DCA) metric formalizes this by rewarding correct predictions with higher precision and tolerating small deviations up to a threshold T. This aligns with information retrieval paradigms where relevance is scored with diminishing returns. The divide-and-conquer batching strategy decomposes long narratives into manageable chunks, enabling better context handling without sacrificing accuracy—this is especially critical when dealing with high-scoring or dense narratives. SportsGen synthesizes adversarial examples that stress-test models' ability to attribute points correctly under varying degrees of ambiguity and symbolic distortion. These primitives together form a robust evaluation framework for assessing narrative-based reasoning systems, particularly in domains like sports analytics where precision matters.
